Question:
How many footnotes have been made in year 1980 and what are the table names of these countries that made the footnotes?
Evidence:
year 1980 refers to Year = 'YR1980';

```sql
SELECT COUNT(T2.Description) FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980' UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT T1.TableName FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980'
```

Evidence:
difficulty refers to diff; most difficult course refers to MAX(diff); student's full names = f_name, l_name;

answer:
```sql
SELECT s.f_name, s.l_name 
FROM student s
JOIN registration r ON s.student_id = r.student_id
JOIN course c ON r.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE c.diff = (SELECT MAX(diff) FROM course)
  AND r.grade = 'A';
```

Question:
Calculate the GPA of the semester for Laughton Antonio.
Evidence:
GPA of the semester = DIVIDE(SUM(MULTIPLY(credit, grade)), SUM(credit)); grade 'A' refers to gpa = 4; grade 'B' refers to gpa = 3; grade 'C' refers to gpa = 2; grade 'D' refers to gpa = 1;

answer:
```sql
SELECT SUM(C.credit * CASE WHEN R.grade = 'A' THEN 4.0 WHEN R.grade = 'B' THEN 3.0 WHEN R.grade = 'C' THEN 2.0 WHEN R.grade = 'D' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / SUM(C.credit) AS gpa
FROM course AS C
JOIN registration AS R ON C.course_id = R.course_id
WHERE R.student_id = (SELECT student_id FROM student WHERE f_name = 'Laughton' AND l_name = 'Antonio');
```

Question:
What is the difference in the average GPA of students who took the hardest and easiest courses?
Evidence:
difference in the average gpa = SUBTRACT(AVG(gpa WHERE MAX(diff)), AVG(gpa where min(diff))); difficulty of the course refers to diff; hardest course refers to MAX(diff); easiest course refers to MIN(diff);

answer:
```sql
SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN r.course_id IN (SELECT course_id FROM course ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 1) THEN s.gpa END) - 
       AVG(CASE WHEN r.course_id IN (SELECT course_id FROM course ORDER BY diff ASC LIMIT 1) THEN s.gpa END) 
FROM registration r 
JOIN student s ON r.student_id = s.student_id;
```

Please give the name of the course in which most numbers of the students got an A. Also, list the full name of the students who got an A in this course.
Evidence:
most number of students got an A refers MAX(COUNT(student_id WHERE grade = 'A')); full name = f_name, l_name; got an A refers to grade = 'A';

answer:
```sql
SELECT c.name, s.f_name, s.l_name 
FROM course c 
JOIN registration r ON c.course_id = r.course_id 
JOIN student s ON r.student_id = s.student_id 
WHERE r.grade = 'A' 
GROUP BY c.course_id, c.name, s.f_name, s.l_name 
ORDER BY COUNT(r.student_id) DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```

Which are the courses with the most number of professors? State the course ID and the level of the course.
Evidence:

```sql

JOIN taughtBy AS t ON c.course_id = t.course_id

ORDER BY COUNT(t.p_id) DESC 
LIMIT 1
```

answer:

```sql
    WHERE person.professor = 1
    GROUP BY taughtBy.p_id
```

```sql
GROUP BY p.p_id, p.hasPosition 
ORDER BY course_count DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```

How many times is the number of keywords in "Refuge: Part 1" episode than "Shield" episode?
Evidence:
"Refuge: Part 1" episode refers to title = 'Refuge: Part 1'; "Shield" episode refers to title = 'Shield'; times = divide(count(keyword where title = 'Refuge: Part 1'), count(keyword where title = 'Shield'))

answer:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(k1.keyword) * 1.0 / COUNT(k2.keyword) AS ratio 
FROM Keyword k1 
JOIN Episode e1 ON k1.episode_id = e1.episode_id 
WHERE e1.title = 'Refuge: Part 1'

CROSS JOIN 

(SELECT COUNT(keyword) 
 FROM Keyword k2 
 JOIN Episode e2 ON k2.episode_id = e2.episode_id 
 WHERE e2.title = 'Shield') AS shield_count;
```

How many episodes are there in the 9th season of Law and Order? Calculate the average number of casts per season of the said series.
Evidence:

answer:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS episode_count, (SELECT COUNT(c.person_id) FROM Credit c JOIN Episode e ON c.episode_id = e.episode_id WHERE e.series = 'Law and Order' AND e.season = 9) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(e.episode_id) FROM Episode e WHERE e.series = 'Law and Order' AND e.season = 9) AS avg_casts_per_season 
FROM Episode 
WHERE series = 'Law and Order' AND season = 9;
```

```sql
GROUP BY e.episode_id, e.title 
ORDER BY COUNT(c.person_id) DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```

Question:
Who is the person who appeared the most in the series? Calculate in percentage how many times he or she appeared.
Evidence:
who refers to name; appear the most refers to max(count(person_id)); percentage = divide(count(person_id where max(count(person_id))), count(person_id)) * 100%

answer:
```sql
SELECT p.name, (COUNT(a.person_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(person_id) FROM Award)) AS percentage 
FROM Person p 
JOIN Award a ON p.person_id = a.person_id 
GROUP BY p.person_id 
ORDER BY percentage DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```

answer:

```sql
FROM Episode E
JOIN Credit C ON E.episode_id = C.episode_id
JOIN Award A ON E.episode_id = A.episode_id
WHERE E.title = 'True North';
```

```sql
SELECT e.title, a.role

  AND a.result = 'Winner' 
  AND a.person_id IN (SELECT person_id FROM Person WHERE name = 'Julia Roberts');
```

Evidence:
American refers to birth_country = 'USA'; cast refers to category = 'Cast'; ratio = divide(count(person_id where birth_country = 'USA'), total(category)) where category = 'Cast'

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN P.birth_country = 'USA' THEN 1 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(C.diff) AS ratio,
    C.role
FROM Credit AS C
JOIN Person AS P ON C.person_id = P.person_id
JOIN Episode ON C.episode_id = Episode.episode_id
WHERE Episode.series = 'Series' AND Episode.episode = 2 AND C.category = 'Cast'
GROUP BY C.role;
```

Evidence:
received award refers to result = 'Winner'; the highest percentage refers to max(percent); average star = divide(sum(stars), count(episode_id))

answer:
```sql
SELECT AVG(V.stars) AS average_stars 
FROM Vote V 
JOIN Award A ON V.episode_id = A.episode_id 
WHERE A.result = 'Winner' 
  AND V.percent = (SELECT MAX(percent) FROM Vote V2 JOIN Award A2 ON V2.episode_id = A2.episode_id WHERE A2.result = 'Winner')
```


Question:
How many footnotes have been made in year 1980 and what are the table names of these countries that made the footnotes?
Evidence:
year 1980 refers to Year = 'YR1980';

```sql
SELECT COUNT(T2.Description) FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980' UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT T1.TableName FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980'
```

Question:
What was the original price of Xerox 1952 ordered by Aimee Bixby on 2014/9/10?
Evidence:
Xerox 1952 is a "Product Name"; ordered by Aimee Bixby refers to "Customer Name" = 'Aimee Bixby'; on 2014/9/10 refers to "Order Date" = date('2014-09-10'); original price refers to DIVIDE(Sales, SUTRACT(1, discount))

answer:
```sql
SELECT (c.Sales / (1 - c.Discount)) AS original_price 
FROM central_superstore AS c
JOIN people AS p ON c."Customer ID" = p."Customer ID" AND c.Region = p.Region
JOIN product AS pr ON c."Product ID" = pr."Product ID" AND c.Region = pr.Region
WHERE p."Customer Name" = 'Aimee Bixby' 
  AND c."Order Date" = '2014-09-10'
  AND pr."Product Name" = 'Xerox 1952';
```

```sql
SELECT (Sales / (1 - Discount)) * Quantity - Profit AS total_cost

WHERE product."Product Name" = 'Xerox 1952' 
  AND people."Customer Name" = 'Aimee Bixby' 
  AND central_superstore."Order Date" = '2014-09-10';
```

```sql
ORDER BY cs."Order Date" DESC
```

Evidence:

answer:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p."Customer ID") 
FROM west_superstore w 
JOIN people p ON w."Customer ID" = p."Customer ID" AND w.Region = p.Region 
JOIN product pr ON w."Product ID" = pr."Product ID" AND w.Region = pr.Region 
WHERE p.City = 'Chicago' 
  AND pr."Product Name" = 'Cardinal EasyOpen D-Ring Binders' 
  AND w.Quantity >= 14;
```

```sql
JOIN product p ON w."Product ID" = p."Product ID" AND w.Region = p.Region

```

Evidence:
name of all the products refers to Product Name; order quantities greater than or equal to 10 refers to COUNT("Order ID") > = 10; slowest delivery refers to "Ship Mode" = 'Standard Class'

answer:
```sql
SELECT p."Product Name"

JOIN product p ON c."Product ID" = p."Product ID" 
WHERE c."Ship Mode" = 'Standard Class' 
GROUP BY p."Product Name"
HAVING SUM(c.Quantity) >= 10;
```

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN p."Category" = 'Office Supplies' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.0) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM central_superstore cs
JOIN product p ON cs."Product ID" = p."Product ID" AND cs.Region = 'Central'
UNION ALL

    (SUM(CASE WHEN p."Category" = 'Office Supplies' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.0) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM south_superstore ss
JOIN product p ON ss."Product ID" = p."Product ID" AND ss.Region = 'South';
```

Calculate the difference between the total sales in the East superstore and the total sales in the West superstore.
Evidence:
East superstore refers to Region = 'East'; West superstore refers to Region = 'West'; difference = subtract(sum(Sales) when Region = 'East', sum(Sales) when Region = 'West')

answer:
```sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN Region = 'East' THEN Sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN Region = 'West' THEN Sales ELSE 0 END) 
FROM east_superstore 
UNION ALL 
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN Region = 'East' THEN Sales ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN Region = 'West' THEN Sales ELSE 0 END) 
FROM west_superstore
```

answer:
```sql
SELECT p."Customer Name" 
FROM people AS p 
JOIN east_superstore AS e ON p."Customer ID" = e."Customer ID" AND p.Region = e.Region 
WHERE p.State = 'Rhode Island' 
  AND p.Segment = 'Corporate' 
  AND e."Order Date" BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31' 
GROUP BY p."Customer Name" 
ORDER BY COUNT(e."Order ID") DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```

Question:
What is the percentage of orders with 0.2 discount in the Central superstore were purchased by customers who live in Texas?
Evidence:
live in Texas refers to State = 'Texas'; percentage = divide(sum(Order ID) when Discount = 0.2, sum(Order ID)) as percentage

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN "Discount" = 0.2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.0) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM central_superstore
JOIN people ON central_superstore."Customer ID" = people."Customer ID" AND central_superstore.Region = people.Region
WHERE people.State = 'Texas';
```

```sql

FROM central_superstore cs
JOIN product p ON cs."Product ID" = p."Product ID" AND cs.Region = p.Region
WHERE cs."Ship Mode" = 'first class' AND cs."Order Date" LIKE '2013%'
```

Evidence:

answer:

```sql
SELECT 
    (COUNT(CASE WHEN "Discount" = 0 THEN 1 END. * 100.0) / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM central_superstore
JOIN people ON central_superstore."Customer ID" = people."Customer ID" AND central_superstore.Region = people.Region
WHERE people.State = 'Indiana' AND central_superstore.Discount = 0;
```

Question:
How many footnotes have been made in year 1980 and what are the table names of these countries that made the footnotes?
Evidence:
year 1980 refers to Year = 'YR1980';

```sql
SELECT COUNT(T2.Description) FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980' UNION ALL SELECT DISTINCT T1.TableName FROM Country AS T1 INNER JOIN FootNotes AS T2 ON T1.CountryCode = T2.Countrycode WHERE T2.Year = 'YR1980'
```

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN e.FirstName = 'Albert' AND e.MiddleInitial = 'I' AND e.LastName = 'Ringer' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.0) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) AS percentage

JOIN Customers c ON s.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN Employees e ON s.SalesPersonID = e.EmployeeID
WHERE s.ProductID = (SELECT ProductID FROM Products WHERE Name = 'ML Bottom Bracket');
```



Question:
Among the sales ID ranges from 1 to 200, what is the percentage of the products with a price ranging from 200 to 300?
Evidence:
sales ID ranges from 1 to 200 refers to SalesID between 1 and 200; percentage = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(SUM(Price between 200 and 300), COUNT(Price)), 1.0);

```sql
FROM Sales s
JOIN Products p ON s.ProductID = p.ProductID
WHERE s.SalesID BETWEEN 1 AND 200;
```

```sql
FROM publisher p
JOIN book b ON p.publisher_id = b.publisher_id
GROUP BY p.publisher_name
ORDER BY COUNT(b.book_id) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
FROM book AS b
```

```sql
ORDER BY b.publication_date ASC
```

International shipping order refers to method_name = 'International'; orders on 2022/11/10 refers to order_date LIKE '2022-11-10%'; percentage = Divide (Sum(order_id  where method_name = 'International'), Count(order_id)) * 100

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    (COUNT(CASE WHEN sm.method_name = 'International' THEN 1 END. * 100.0) / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM "cust_order" co
JOIN shipping_method sm ON co.shipping_method_id = sm.method_id
WHERE co.order_date LIKE '2022-11-10%'
```

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "cust_order" CO 
JOIN address A ON CO.dest_address_id = A.address_id 
JOIN country C ON A.country_id = C.country_id 
WHERE C.country_name = 'Iran' 
  AND CO.order_date LIKE '2022%'
```

Question:
What is the full name of the customer who ordered the most books of all time?
Evidence:
customer who ordered the most book refers to customer_id where Max(count(order_id)); full name refers to first_name, last_name

answer:
```sql
SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name 
FROM customer c 
JOIN cust_order co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id 
GROUP BY c.customer_id 
ORDER BY COUNT(co.order_id) DESC 
LIMIT 1;
```


Question:
What is the total shipping cost of all the orders made by Page Holsey? Indicate how many of the said orders were ordered in 2022.
Evidence:
shipping cost refers to cost; ordered in 2022 refers to order_date LIKE '2022%'

answer:
```sql
SELECT SUM(s.cost) AS total_shipping_cost, COUNT(*) AS order_count_in_2022 
FROM "cust_order" co 
JOIN shipping_method s ON co.shipping_method_id = s.method_id 
JOIN customer cust ON co.customer_id = cust.customer_id 
WHERE cust.first_name = 'Page' AND cust.last_name = 'Holsey' 
  AND co.order_date LIKE '2022%';
```

Question:
List the author's and publisher's name of the book published on July 10, 1997.
Evidence:
author's name refers to author_name; publisher's name refers to publisher_name; book published on July 10, 1997 refers to publication_date LIKE '1997-07-10'

answer:
```sql
SELECT a.author_name, p.publisher_name 
FROM book b 
JOIN book_author ba ON b.book_id = ba.book_id 
JOIN author a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id 
JOIN publisher p ON b.publisher_id = p.publisher_id 
WHERE b.publication_date = '1997-07-10'
```

Question:
Calculate the total price of books ordered by customer named Lucas Wyldbore.
Evidence:
total price refers to Sum(price); full name is composed of first name, last name

```sql
SELECT SUM(b.price) AS total_price 
FROM "cust_order" co
JOIN customer c ON co.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN "order_line" ol ON co.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN book b ON ol.book_id = b.book_id
WHERE c.first_name = 'Lucas' AND c.last_name = 'Wyldbore';
```

Question:
List the email of customers that bought the book titled Switch on the Night.
Evidence:
"Switch on the Night" is the title

answer:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.email 
FROM customer c
JOIN "cust_order" co ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
JOIN "order_line" ol ON co.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN book b ON ol.book_id = b.book_id
WHERE b.title = 'Switch on the Night';
```

List the author's name of the books published by Abrams.
Evidence:
"Abrams" is the publisher_name; author's name refers to author_name

```sql
FROM author a

WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Abrams';
```

Question:
In books authored by Abraham Lincoln, what is the percentage of the books published in 1992?
Evidence:
"Abraham Lincoln" is the author_name; published in 1992 refers to publication_date LIKE '1992%'; percentage = Divide (Sum(publication_date LIKE '1992%'), Count(publication_date)) * 100

answer:
```sql
SELECT 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN b.publication_date LIKE '1992%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END.0) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) AS percentage
FROM book b
JOIN book_author ba ON b.book_id = ba.book_id
JOIN author a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id
WHERE a.author_name = 'Abraham Lincoln';
```

Question:
Among the books published in 2004, list the name of the publisher of books with number of pages greater than 70% of the average number of pages of all books.
Evidence:
published in 2004 refers to publication_date LIKE '2004%'; books with number of pages greater than 70% of the average number of pages refers to num_pages > Multiply(Avg(num_pages), 0.7); name of publisher refers to publisher_name

answer:
```sql
SELECT p.publisher_name 
FROM book b 
JOIN publisher p ON b.publisher_id = p.publisher_id 
WHERE b.publication_date LIKE '2004%' 
  AND b.num_pages > (SELECT AVG(num_pages) * 0.7 FROM book)
```

Provide the authors and titles of the books which have more than 3000 pages.
Evidence:
authors refers to author_name; more than 3000 pages refers to num_pages > 3000

answer:
```sql
SELECT a.author_name, b.title 
FROM book AS b 
JOIN book_author AS ba ON b.book_id = ba.book_id 
JOIN author AS a ON ba.author_id = a.author_id 
WHERE b.num_pages > 3000;
```

How many footnotes have been made in year 1980 and what are the table names of these countries that made the footnotes?

year 1980 refers to Year = 'YR1980';

```sql

```

Question:
How many percent of orders in 2020 used international shipping?
Evidence:
international shipping refers to method_name = 'International'; orders in 2020 refers to order_date = '2020%'; percentage = Divide (Sum(method_name = 'International'), Count(order_id)) * 100

answer:
```sql
SELECT (COUNT(CASE WHEN sm.method_name = 'International' THEN 1 END. * 100.0) / COUNT(*)) AS percentage 
FROM "cust_order" co
JOIN shipping_method sm ON co.shipping_method_id = sm.method_id
WHERE co.order_date LIKE '2020%'
```
